author: reek
body: A dashboard turns query results into one self-contained HTML page. Every chart is inline SVG built from integer arithmetic, every style lives in one style block, and nothing on the page references an external script, sheet, font, or image, so the same text renders identically wherever it lands: served by the native service, served by the emitted barbarian service, or saved to a file and opened by hand. This chapter knows nothing about how a query executes. It treats a LensQuery as an opaque request and a QueryResult as the answer, and the one function that runs queries delegates to lens-run and hands the results straight to the static renderer, so a service that executes queries its own way can call the static entry with results it computed itself.

author: reek
body: Three chart kinds cover v1. A bar chart draws one measure as vertical bars, one per row, with the first result column as the category. A stacked bar keeps the first column on the x axis and stacks the remaining measure columns as colored segments. A table prints the result verbatim, header row and all. The constructors carry an Ld prefix because constructor names are program-wide.

author: reek
body: A tile is one titled chart over one query. A dashboard is a titled list of tiles, rendered in declaration order into a grid.

author: reek
body: Every piece of text that lands in markup goes through ld-escape: titles, axis labels, table cells, error messages, legend names. The walk compares each character as text rather than by code, because character codes are CCE inside the compiler and the three characters HTML cares about must be recognized by identity, not by a barbarian code point.

author: reek
body: Small builders for the SVG vocabulary the charts use, each returning one element followed by a newline so the page stays readable and diffable. Text content arrives pre-escaped; attribute values here are integers and palette colors, which never need escaping.

author: reek
body: Five gridlines, at zero and at each multiple of the step up to the axis top, each with its round-number label right-aligned into the left margin. The two solid axis lines draw after the grid so they sit on top of it.

author: reek
body: A fixed palette of six colors, cycled when a stacked chart carries more series than the palette has entries. Single bars take the first color.

author: reek
body: The charts read a QueryResult positionally: column zero is the category, the columns after it are the numeric series. Numbers come out through val-to-integer and display text through val-to-text, the engine's own renderings, and display text is escaped on the way out. The maximum scans find the axis top: the single-column maximum for plain bars, the maximum row total for stacked bars.

author: reek
body: The plot width divides evenly into one slot per category, each bar takes three fifths of its slot, and the remainder splits into equal gaps on either side. Every position is integer division, so the emitted coordinates are exact and pinnable by a test.

author: reek
body: One bar per row: the value scales into the plot, the bar rises from the baseline, the value prints just above the bar, and the category prints under the baseline. An empty result renders a visible notice instead of an empty frame.

author: reek
body: A stacked bar accumulates the series values bottom up. Each segment takes its top and bottom edges from the running total scaled into the plot, so the segments tile the bar exactly and rounding never opens a gap between them; a segment whose rounded height is zero is simply skipped. The axis scales to the largest row total. A legend under the chart names each series in its color, taking the names from the result schema.

author: reek
body: A table prints the result as it stands: a header row from the schema's column names, then one row per data row, every cell escaped.

author: reek
body: A tile is a section carrying its escaped title and its body. A failed result never disappears: the tile renders the error message where the chart would have been, in the loud style the design demands of every failure a dashboard could otherwise hide.

author: reek
body: The page is complete and self-contained: doctype, title, one style block, a heading, and the tile grid. The style is a light theme on a system font stack, and every rule is spelled here rather than fetched, because a dashboard that needs a network to look right is not self-contained. The static entry renders pre-computed results in tile order, one result per tile, and a tile whose result is missing renders as a failed tile rather than vanishing. The catalog entry runs each tile's query through lens-run and hands the results to the static entry, so both targets share every line of rendering.

author: reek
body: The explore page turns the model's governed vocabulary into a form a browser can post back: one checkbox per dimension, one checkbox per measure with the measure's signed-off description beside it, because seeing what a measure means before picking it is the point of Lens, a numeric limit defaulting to zero for no limit, and a submit button. The form posts to /explore rather than encoding a query string, because the service's path seam never sees a query string. The incoming selection threads back in so the boxes an analyst checked stay checked on the result page. Every name and description lands in markup through ld-escape; the names are governed kebab-case identifiers, so the escaped text is also safe inside a quoted attribute.

author: reek
body: A run's answer renders inside one tile-styled section under the form: the result as a table always, through the same body renderer the dashboard tiles use, so a failed plan shows its diagnostics in the same loud error style, and a bar chart besides when the shape charts well, which is exactly one selected dimension, at least one measure, and at least one row. The executed SQL prints under its own small heading whenever a statement ran, escaped like every other piece of data-derived text; a refused plan runs no SQL and the empty text suppresses the heading.

author: reek
body: The explore page is self-contained in the same discipline as the dashboard: one style block, inline SVG, no external reference. Its style is the dashboard's sheet with the form rules appended, kept as an extension rather than an edit so the dashboard page's bytes never move. Two entries share every line: the bare entry renders the form with no results section, which is the GET answer, and the run entry renders the form with the results of the query the analyst posted. The page is rebuilt from the model on every request and none of it outlives the reply.
